name: Cost Differences: Over-Garage ADU vs Side or Rear ADU Addition

mainEntity.name: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County estimate costs differently for over-garage ADUs versus side or rear additions?
mainEntity.text: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County estimate costs differently for over-garage ADUs versus side or rear additions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cost estimating for ADU additions in Los Angeles County varies significantly between building over a garage and extending at the side or rear of a home. Over‑garage ADUs typically involve reinforcing the existing garage structure or adding new posts, beams, and footings to safely support the added weight. This kind of work requires more structural engineering time, longer inspections, and more invasive construction, often leading to higher per‑square‑foot costs. Roof removal and temporary weather protection also increase labor. In contrast, side or rear additions usually sit on new foundations designed specifically for the ADU, which can be simpler structurally but may require more site work, such as grading, retaining walls, or trenching for utilities. Access plays a big role: tight side yards can mean more hand‑digging and material handling costs. Utility runs—sewer, water, electrical, and gas—may be shorter and cheaper for an over‑garage ADU if it is near existing service points, or more expensive if everything has to be routed across the property. Experienced ADU additions contractors will break out structural, site work, finishes, and utility costs separately, then explain how design choices like unit size, bathroom count, and ceiling height affect the budget. Request this level of detail so you can compare options realistically.
acceptedAnswer.description: Over‑garage ADUs usually cost more per square foot than side or rear additions because they require stronger garage foundations, new floor structures, and more complex structural engineering. Side or rear additions may need less structural work but can trigger larger site work, grading, or utility rerouting costs depending on access.
